title: Orecchiette con Broccoli
subtitle: Pugliese pasta with broccoli and anchovy
excerpt: Short pasta cooked with broccoli until the florets half-dissolve into the sauce, seasoned with anchovy, garlic, and chilli. The broccoli becomes the sauce, a technique from Puglia.

recipe.sourceNotes: Orecchiette con cime di rapa (turnip tops) is the canonical Pugliese dish. Broccoli is the accessible substitute used outside Puglia, and the technique is identical: the vegetables go into the pasta water and cook until soft enough to become part of the sauce when tossed with the pasta. Anchovies are the seasoning, not the flavour.

content.text: The Pugliese technique for orecchiette with broccoli is to cook the broccoli in the pasta water until it is very soft, then add the pasta, and let everything cook together so the florets break down and cling to the ridged pasta. The anchovy in the oil gives backbone without tasting of fish. This is one of the best things you can make from a head of broccoli.

items.preparation: cut into small florets including the tender stems
toasted golden in a dry pan

content.text: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Add the broccoli florets and cook for 5 minutes until tender. Add the pasta and cook until al dente. Reserve a large cup of pasta water before draining everything together.

While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the anchovies and cook for 2 minutes, pressing them until they dissolve. Add the garlic and chilli and cook for 2 minutes.

Add the drained pasta and broccoli to the pan. Toss vigorously over medium heat, breaking up the broccoli florets with a spoon so they coat the pasta. Add pasta water a splash at a time until you have a thick, clingy sauce.
Taste for salt and pepper. Serve in warm bowls with the toasted breadcrumbs scattered over the top. No cheese.
